summary: The recorded-dive stages match skills/mind-meld.md closely: every spec role, detail, risk, step and glossary entry has a source line. The two diagram-only problems are the "learning IDE" label, which the skill doc never uses, and the verify-to-view gate, which the source states as a gate on trusting the evidence rather than on opening the viewer. The largest gap is what is not shown: the default static map mode has no stage, and the sandbox test gate, secret redaction and no-download rules are absent.

code.overview: Most of the recorded dive is code: scripts/mind-meld.ts is the CLI and reference adapter, scripts/mind-meld-sandbox.ts runs code in Docker, scripts/mind-meld-schema.ts validates the bundle, and scripts/mind-meld-viewer.ts and scripts/mind-meld-pages.ts render it. That code only covers the tiny reference example (scripts/mind-meld-example.ts); adapters for a real stack are left to each repo. Choosing the question and writing the narration are done by the agent from the skill text. The default static map (scripts/mind-meld-map.ts, scripts/mind-meld-langs.ts) is also code, but this diagram has no stage for it.

refs.title: index(): the reference index adapter
refs.explain: It reads the five mind-meld source files into memory. It parses the example file with the TypeScript compiler and makes one node per exported function, with its start and end line. It then walks each function body and records a static call edge wherever one indexed function calls another. The result is a version 1 bundle with the source text, a hash per file and no runs yet.
refs.why: This is the "index adapter" half of the stage: nodes, static call edges, source bytes and hashes. It only indexes the reference example, so a real repo still has to write its own.

refs.anchor: if (target !== 'damage' || Object.keys(fakes).join(',') !== 'save' || fakes.save !== 'memory') throw new Error('reference piece supports damage with save: memory');
refs.title: run_flow / run_piece: only registered targets run
refs.explain: run_flow accepts one entry name, combat, and throws for anything else. run_piece accepts only the damage target with the fake policy save: memory, and throws otherwise. Both then hand off to the shared run function.
refs.why: This is the rule that an execution adapter runs only targets it has registered. Without it a question could be turned into an arbitrary command.

refs.anchor: if (!isAdapter(adapter)) throw new Error(`${REPO_ADAPTERS}/${f}: default export needs name, extensions and facts()`);
refs.title: loadAdapters: a repo adds its own language adapter
refs.explain: It looks for .mind-meld/languages in the repo and imports every .ts, .js or .mjs file there. Each default export must have a name, extensions and a facts function, or loading fails with the file name. The repo adapters are placed before the four built-in ones, so a repo can replace a built-in for an extension.
refs.why: This is how repo-specific code plugs in for the static map. Note it serves the map command; the recorded dive has no equivalent loader, so its adapters are hand-written exports like the reference.

refs.title: sandboxArgs: the locked-down docker run command
refs.explain: It builds the argument list for docker run. The list pins the image by digest and forbids pulling, turns the network off, makes the root read-only, drops all capabilities, runs as an unprivileged user and caps processes, memory and CPU. The source file is mounted read-only and the only writable place is a small temporary /work. The command inside the container is wrapped in timeout so it is killed at the deadline.
refs.why: These flags are the sandbox the "Record real runs" stage promises. Dropping any of them would let recorded code reach the network or write to the repo.

refs.anchor: export function runSandbox(source: string, args: string[], timeoutMs = MELD_LIMIT_MS, expectedHash?: string): string {
refs.title: runSandbox: snapshot, run, clean up
refs.explain: It rejects a timeout outside the allowed limit and makes a unique container name and a temporary folder. It copies the source into that folder as a read-only file, checking the hash first if one was given, and runs the container. Whether the run worked or not, it then force-removes only the container with that name and deletes the temporary folder. A cleanup error or the run error is thrown; otherwise the output is returned.
refs.why: This carries out one recorded run and guarantees nothing is left behind. There is no fallback path: if Docker fails, the run fails.

refs.anchor: const event: Event = { id: String(events.length), node, parent, durationMs: 0, input, output: '', changes: [] };
refs.title: span: how an event gets recorded
refs.explain: Each instrumented function calls span with its name, its parent event id and its input. span appends a new event, runs the real work, then stores the output and the measured duration on that event. The script prints the output and the full event list as JSON when it ends.
refs.why: This is where the recording comes from: real calls inside the container, with the parent taken from the actual call. The reference example is the only code instrumented this way.

refs.title: Sandbox probes: no writes, no network, timeout kills
refs.explain: The first test runs a probe script in the real sandbox that tries to overwrite its own source and open a network connection, and expects both to fail while a save in the temporary folder works. The second runs an endless loop with a 1.5 second limit and expects the sandbox to fail it. Both run only when RUN_MIND_MELD_SANDBOX is set; CI sets it in the mind-meld-sandbox job.
refs.why: The skill says an execution adapter may not be called working until these probes pass. They are the proof that the sandbox flags do what they claim.

refs.anchor: return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify({ version: 1, snapshotHash, compiler: compiler?.version ?? null, image: MELD_IMAGE, mode, inputs: inputs(value), fakes: { save: 'memory' } })).digest('hex');
refs.title: cacheKey and run: cache a recording by what could change it
refs.explain: cacheKey hashes the source snapshot hash, compiler version, image, mode, inputs and fake policy. run checks the inputs, indexes the source and looks the key up in an in-memory cache, returning a copy on a hit. On a miss it runs the sandbox, stamps the result with the key and snapshot hash, and fails if the source changed while it ran. The result is validated as part of a bundle before it is cached.
refs.why: This is the rule that a recording is never reused under a new source hash. The cache lives only for one process; nothing is stored on disk.

refs.anchor: if (r.snapshotHash !== b.snapshotHash) throw new Error('run belongs to another source snapshot');
refs.title: validateBundle: the executable schema
refs.explain: It requires version 1, then checks the sources for size, the hashes against the source text, the nodes against the sources and the static edges against the nodes. For each run it checks the fields, that the run carries the bundle snapshot hash, that its key is unique and its entry is an indexed node, and then validates its events. Any failed check throws.
refs.why: Every command validates a bundle with this before it renders, diffs or prints it. Without it a hand-edited or mismatched bundle could be shown as evidence.

refs.anchor: if (!file || file.startsWith('/') || file.includes('\\') || file.split('/').some(p => !p || p === '.' || p === '..') || file.includes('\0')) throw new Error('invalid source path');
refs.title: sourceManifest and validateManifest: the snapshot identity
refs.explain: sourceManifest hashes each source file and then hashes the sorted list of those hashes into one snapshot hash. validateManifest repeats the work on a bundle it is given: it rejects absolute or escaping paths, recomputes every file hash, and compares the recomputed snapshot hash with the one in the bundle.
refs.why: This binds the embedded source text to the hash that runs are stamped with. It is what makes "this run belongs to this source" checkable.

refs.anchor: export function diff(a: MeldRun, b: MeldRun): { pathA: string[]; pathB: string[]; outputA: string; outputB: string; changesA: unknown[]; changesB: unknown[] } {
refs.title: diff: compare two recorded runs
refs.explain: For each of the two runs it lists the nodes its events visited in order, its output, and all state changes its events recorded. It returns the six lists side by side and judges nothing.
refs.why: This is the diff operation of the bundle stage: paths, outputs and state mutations from each run. The agent reads the difference; the code only lays it out.

refs.anchor: if (!path.startsWith(base + sep) || sourceHash(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')) !== hash) throw new Error(`stale source snapshot: ${file}`);
refs.title: verifySnapshot: does the recording still match the checkout?
refs.explain: It validates the bundle, then resolves each recorded file path inside the chosen checkout root. If a path resolves outside the root, or the file on disk hashes differently from the recording, it throws "stale source snapshot" with the file name.
refs.why: This is the verify step. Without it an old tour could be read as a statement about today's code.

refs.anchor:
Source snapshot: ${bundle.snapshotHash}. Offline capture; current checkout freshness is unknown. Run the CLI verify command before relying on this tour.

refs.title: renderViewer: the one-file offline page
refs.explain: It validates the bundle and embeds it, with the viewer function, as one inline script. The page carries a Content-Security-Policy that allows only that script and that style by hash and blocks all network connections. The page text states the snapshot hash and that checkout freshness is unknown offline. The same viewer script holds the run selector, the Previous and Next step buttons and the state-key filter.
refs.why: This is the view command that writes tour.html. The policy is why the page needs no server and cannot fetch anything.

refs.anchor: ? `The reader is learning how ${entries.join(', ')} works in this repo from recorded runs (snapshot ${bundle.snapshotHash}).`
refs.title: bundleToSpec: the same evidence as a markdown page
refs.explain: It validates the bundle and turns each indexed function into a page entry with its source link, static calls, recorded calls and source excerpt. If there are runs, the arrows are only the recorded parent-to-child calls; if there are none, the arrows are the static calls, labelled as not observed. The spec is checked before it is returned for rendering.
refs.why: This is the pages command. Every line comes from an indexed span or a recorded event, so the page cannot contain narration or invented steps.

promptOnly.what: The agent names the question, finds the real entry point, test and state owner by reading source, and picks a flow to record; no script helps choose.
The agent writes the narration from the two prompts in the skill and must cite file:line and event ids; the code only steps through recorded events in the viewer and never checks or stores narration.
Adapters for a real stack (Rust, Godot and so on) are written by hand in the child repo following the contract table; scaffold ships only the reference adapter for its own example.
